title: Prefixcache tenant fingerprinting, safe-resume strategy, and targeted sweep
creator: Marisol Reyes
description: Summary: During a capacity incident on 2026-02-07 we observed sustained prefixcache occupancy growth tied to tenant-prefetch contamination. A small number of tenants caused prefetch churn and eviction thrashing that led to increased CPU and OOM risk on GPU nodes. Root cause analysis indicates a combination of aggressive prefetch heuristics + a race in the tenant namespace tagging path that allowed stale prefetch keys to be attributed to the wrong tenant under heavy load. This ticket implements a robust mitigation and recovery plan that: (1) fingerprints prefetch/kv entries at write time to a tenant-stable token, (2) introduces a safe-resume mechanism to avoid re-inserting contaminated prefixes during node restarts, and (3) provides a targeted sweep utility to recover affected tenants without global cache flushes.
acceptance_criteria: Fingerprint applied: every prefetch/insert records a tenant-stable fingerprint/token and is verifiable in telemetry
Safe-resume implemented: node restart path validates fingerprint token and rejects replays of mismatched tenant-prefetch entries
Targeted sweep tool: can evict contaminated keys for a single tenant with <30s outage to that tenant and no impact to others
Telemetry: dashboards show tenant-level prefetched-entry churn rate, fingerprint mismatch rate, and eviction-thrash metric with alerts
Canary rollout: feature enabled in staging and one dedicated region, run for 48 hours with no CPU/memory regressions
comments: 2026-02-08 - Initial triage: incident declared. Observed large increase in prefixcache insert rate correlated with two tenant IDs. Temporary mitigations: throttled prefetch for candidates >10k inserts/min (hotfix). - Marisol

2026-02-09 - Deep dive: repro across internal load generator. Found race where prefetch write path read tenant id from ephemeral context that could be clobbered during async scheduling. Hypothesis: stale context -> wrong-tenant attribution. - Ajay

2026-02-11 - Design sync: decided on a fingerprint token approach rather than moving to synchronous tenant resolution. Trade-offs: fingerprint adds 8 bytes per entry but avoids adding latency to hot path. Agreed to gated rollout. - Meeting notes: Confluence/Prefix-Fingerprint-Design

2026-02-14 - Implementation update: started instrumenting write path (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/prefixcache/pull/1987). Added unit tests for token generation and race simulation harness. - Ajay

2026-02-18 - Review feedback from runtime team: request to add an LRU-safe metadata slot to avoid extra allocations; opted for fixed-size token in header. Also add a checksum to detect cross-tenant replays. - Review by Priya and Tomas

2026-02-20 - Telemetry plan: new metrics added to infra-metrics: prefetched_entries_total_by_tenant, fingerprint_mismatch_count, targeted_sweep_duration_seconds. Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/prefixcache/tenant-fingerprint

2026-02-22 - Targeted sweep tool: initial implementation as an offline job that reads tenant fingerprint index and issues TTL-evict commands. PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/pull/412. Ran tool in staging against seeded contamination; sweep removed 98% of contaminated keys within 12s for test tenant. - Ops

2026-02-24 - Canary plan: rollout to staging cluster, then dedicated-us-east-1 region for 48h. Fallback: feature flag to revert fingerprint validation and auto-run sweep. Rollout doc: Confluence/Prefix-Fingerprint-Rollout

2026-02-26 - Post-canary notes: small perf impact observed on 95th percentile insert latency (+2.3ms). Team decided acceptable given P1 safety gains. Optimization task to reduce allocation overhead scheduled (ENG-272110). - Ajay

2026-02-28 - Next steps: harden safe-resume to cover mixed-version clusters; implement cross-tenant audit job to surface any remaining contamination; prepare runbook for on-call with step-by-step targeted sweep instructions. - Marisol
